questions.question: With reference to atmospheric pressure, what is the alveolar pressure at the end of normal inspiration (in cms of H2O)?
questions.explanation:
At the end of inspiration, the alveolar pressure is zero with reference to the atmospheric pressure.
Whenever alveolar pressure equals atmospheric pressure, alveolar pressure is said to be zero. This
happens when no air is moving in or out of the lungs.
During inspiration, the diaphragm contracts, causing the volume of the thorax to increase. As lung
volume increases, the pressure in the lungs must decrease. (Boyle's law states that P x V is
constant at a given temperature.) Halfway through inspiration, the alveolar pressure falls below
atmospheric pressure (-1 cm H20). The pressure gradient between the atmosphere ‘and the alveoli
drives airflow into the lung. Air flows into the lungs until, at the end of inspiration, alveolar
pressure is once again equal to the atmospheric pressure; ihe pressure gradient between the
atmosphere and the alveoli has dissipated, and airflow. mbe'the lungs eéases.
During expiration, alveolar pressure rises to about ¥1 cm of H20. a 1

questions.question: A man inspires 1000ml from a spirometer. The intrapleural pressure was -4cm H2O before inspiration and -12cm H2O at the end of inspiration. What is the compliance of lungs?(ml/cm H2O)?
questions.explanation:
Compliance is change in volume per unit change in pressure.
° C= AV/AP
In this case,
AV= 1000 mL
AP= -12-(-4) = -8 cm of H20
The minus sign indicates that the pressure has fallen by 8cms of H20 at the end of inspiration
Therefore the compliance is,
C= 1000/8= 125 mL/cm of H20

questions.question: A 22-year-old woman has pulmonary compliance of 0.2 L/cm H2O and an alveolar pressure of 4 cmH2O and an intrapleural pressure of -5 cmH2O at the beginning of inspiration. What is the transpulmonary pressure (in cmH2O) when this woman inhales 600mL of air ?

wah ~ oe
The transpulmonary pressure would be 12 emH2Q when she inhales 600mL.of air.
Transpulmonary pressure (Ptp) is the difference between alveolar pressure (Palv) and intrapleural
pressure (Pip). It is given by the formula: Ptp = Palv-Pip. Inspiration caisés a negative change in
both the Palv and Pip. Lung complianeg is the extent to which the dings will expand for each unit
increase in transpulmonary pressure. ‘ tot
In a normal adult, the pulmonary compligi¢e is 0.2 Liem#20 or 200 mL/cemH20 of both lungs
together. Hence, expanding the lungs Py. 200 mL of inspired air will require an increase in Ptp by
1cm H20. oe ee

Intrapleural pressure at the beginning of inspiration = -5 cmH20

Step 1: Calculate the initial transpulmonary pressure (Ptp).
Transpulmonary pressure = Alveolar pressure - Intrapleural pressure; Initial transpulmonary
pressure = 4 cmH20 - (-5 cmH20) = 9 cmH20
Step 2: Use the lung compliance formula to find the change in transpulmonary pressure.
Lung compliance = Change in volume / Change in transpulmonary pressure.
Pulmonary compliance is 0.2 L/cemH20 or 200 mL/emH20. Hence, to expand the lungs by 200
mL of inspired air, it will require an increase in Ptp by 1 cm H20. So, for 600 ml inspired air, the
compliance is = 600 mL/ 200 mL/cm H20 = 3 cmH20
Step 3: Calculate the transpulmonary pressure (Ptp) after inhaling 600mL of air.
During inspiration, the alveolar pressure (Palv) decreases, and the intrapleural pressure (Pip)
becomes more negative.
Final transpulmonary pressure = Initial transpulmonary pressure + change in transpulmonary
pressure; Final transpulmonary pressure = 9 cmH20 + 3 cmH20 = 12 emH20.

questions.question: In the pressure-volume graph shown below, compliance of lung is represented by ______.
questions.explanation:
In the given pressure-volume graph:
- A— Compliance of chest
¢ B— Compliance of lung
¢ C— Compliance of lung and chest wall
The equilibrium position is at functional residual capacity (FRC), where the expanding force on
the chest wall is exactly equal to the collapsing force on the lungs. FRC is also known as relaxation
volume and represents the amount of air remaining in the lungs at the end of normal expiration.

At the point where volume= FRC,
« Intraalveolar pressure is equal to atmospheric pressure and considered as zero.
« Intrapleural pressure is negative (-2.5 mmHg)
¢ Transpulmonary pressure = Intraalveolar pressure — intrapleural pressure = 0 — (-2.5 mmHg) =
+2.5 mmHg.
For compliance of lung — Pressure considered is Transpulmonary pressure. So at FRC,
Transpulmonary pressure is positive (+2.5 mmHg). Hence, B indicates compliance of lung.
For compliance of chest wall — Pressure considered is intrapleural — atmospheric pressure. At
FRC, this value is -2.5 mmHg. Hence, A represents compliance of the chest wall.
When the volume is FRC, the combined lung and chest-wall curve intersects the xtaxis atan
airway pressure of zero. Hence, C represents the combined chest wall and lung compliance.

questions.question: The following diagram shows the depth of respiration of a 45-year old man who suffered a head injury in an automobile accident. Identify the pattern of breathing.
questions.explanation:
oo —
The pattern of breathing seen in the image is Cheyne-Stokes breathing. In this case, the person
breathes deeply for a short interval and then breathes slightly or not for an additional interval.
This pattern repeats itself about every minute.’ ° _ ao
It is the most common type of periodic breathing seen-fhost commonly in patients with heart
failure and uremia, also seen in patients with brain disease and duting sleep in normal
individuals. ~ _ a
This increased response oceijes apparently tue to the disruption of neural pathways that normally
inhibit respiration. In such an individual, increased sensitivity to CO2 causes relative
hyperventilation, lowering the arterial Pco2. During the resultant apnoea, the arterial Pco2 rises
again to normal, but the respiratory mechanisms again over-responds to CO2. Breathing ceases,
and the cycle repeats. we ae
